memory_update.text: Direct HBM producer coverage should include MU, Samsung Electronics OTC SSNLF, and SK hynix OTC HXSCF / possible ADR-status watch. These are the highest-priority public-market mappings for this node.

HBM node exposure is not limited to memory makers; meaningful second-order chokepoints include HBM process equipment, DRAM EUV, advanced packaging, probe cards, metrology / inspection, controller IP, and downstream AI accelerator customers.

Important non-U.S. or harder-to-access HBM supply-chain names not fully captured in this U.S.-listed screen may include Japanese / Korean / Taiwanese materials, substrate, bonding, and test-equipment suppliers; further localization pass needed.

CDNS and AMD have relevant HBM exposure but were not included in the 15-candidate cap; keep them as overflow candidates for a larger universe because Cadence has HBM IP and AMD is a downstream HBM-heavy accelerator customer.

For falsification, downgrade the HBM chokepoint if supplier capacity additions outpace accelerator demand, HBM4 yields improve faster than expected across all three memory makers, or AI accelerator roadmaps shift materially toward lower-HBM architectures.

node: HBM, advanced DRAM, and AI memory supply
summary: Expanded U.S.-accessible public universe for the HBM / advanced memory chokepoint. The strongest direct exposures are the three memory producers with U.S. listings or OTC access: Micron, SK hynix, and Samsung Electronics. Second-order exposure clusters around DRAM / HBM wafer-fab equipment, EUV lithography, advanced packaging and test, probe / metrology, HBM controller IP, and downstream AI accelerator customers whose shipment ramps depend on qualified HBM supply. This is a research universe only, not a recommendation list.
